Let \(V=[v_1\ v_2\ v_3\ v_4\ v_5]\). Then
\[
|\det V|^2=\det(V^T V),
\]
so we maximize the determinant of the Gram matrix \(G=(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)\).

The matrix \(G\) has diagonal entries \(1\), cyclic adjacent entries \(1/2\), and five remaining entries
\[
x_i=\langle v_i,v_{i+2}\rangle.
\]
The feasible set of such Gram matrices is compact, so a maximum exists. Since there is a positive definite feasible example, a determinant-maximizer may be taken positive definite. For any cyclic permutation \(P\), \(PGP^T\) has the same determinant and satisfies the same constraints. By concavity of \(\log\det\),
\[
\log\det\left(\frac15\sum_{k=0}^4 P^kG(P^T)^k\right)
\ge \frac15\sum_{k=0}^4 \log\det(P^kG(P^T)^k)
=\log\det G.
\]
Thus a maximizer exists with all distance-two inner products equal, say \(x\).

So \(G\) is the circulant matrix with first row
\[
(1,\tfrac12,x,x,\tfrac12).
\]
Its eigenvalues are
\[
\lambda_0=2+2x,
\]
\[
\lambda_1=\lambda_4=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{4}-\frac{\sqrt5+1}{2}x,
\]
\[
\lambda_2=\lambda_3=\frac{3-\sqrt5}{4}+\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}x.
\]
Hence
\[
\det G=\lambda_0\lambda_1^2\lambda_2^2.
\]
Positive semidefiniteness gives
\[
-\frac{\sqrt5-1}{4}\le x\le \frac{\sqrt5+1}{4}.
\]
The endpoints give determinant \(0\), so we maximize inside the interval.

For the interior maximum, differentiate:
\[
\frac{d}{dx}\log\det G
=
\frac1{1+x}
-\frac{\sqrt5+1}{\lambda_1}
+\frac{\sqrt5-1}{\lambda_2}.
\]
Setting this equal to \(0\) simplifies to
\[
4x^2+2x-1=0,
\]
so
\[
x=\frac{-1+\sqrt5}{4}
\]
is the only feasible interior critical point. At this value,
\[
\lambda_0=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad
\lambda_1=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{4},\qquad
\lambda_2=\frac{3-\sqrt5}{2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\det G
=
\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}
\left(\frac{1+\sqrt5}{4}\right)^2
\left(\frac{3-\sqrt5}{2}\right)^2
=\frac1{16}.
\]
Thus
\[
|\det V|=\sqrt{\det G}=\frac14.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac14}
\]
